title: Check yourself: Assembling a prompt in cache-friendly order

questions.stem: Scenario: Egret Support's request holds fixed rules, a conversation history at priority 5 and marketing blurbs at priority 1. It exceeds its token budget by a small margin. What does the assembler do?

options.text: Truncates the end of the rules until the whole request fits within the budget
options.says: Ruled out because "The static modules are never dropped".

options.text: Drops the conversation history first, because it is the largest block of the three
options.says: Ruled out because "the assembler drops the lowest first", by priority and not by size.

options.text: Refuses the request at once, since it is over budget by any amount at all
options.says: Ruled out because refusal is for when "only static modules remain and they still exceed the budget, the assembler refuses the request".

options.text: Sheds the least important block first, stopping as soon as it fits
options.says: The lowest-priority dynamic block goes first, and the assembler climbs only while the request is still over.

origin.section: A budget drops the least useful context first

questions.stem: Scenario: Heron Retail has four teams that each write the support prompt by hand as one string, with a slightly different order, and the cache hit rate is low. Which change helps most?

options.text: A reminder in the team wiki that the policy text ought to come first in the prompt
options.says: Ruled out because a reminder leaves the order to each caller, where "the assembler decides the order and callers cannot".

options.text: A longer cache lifetime, so that the different strings are all kept for longer
options.says: Ruled out because "Two requests share a cache entry only when everything up to the breakpoint is identical", and a longer lifetime does not make the strings identical.

options.text: A standard header that every team adds to the start of its own prompt
options.says: Ruled out because a header does not fix the order that follows it: "The order is the same every time" only when one assembler decides it.

options.text: A single assembler that arranges named modules, with callers passing only values
options.says: One assembler fixes the order, so every team's prefix matches.

origin.section: A request is modules, not a string
